title: Relative finite presentation of patched modules over a flat ambient algebra
statement: Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings, let $B\to A$ be a ring homomorphism, and put $I=\ker(A'\to A)$ and $R=B\times_A A'=\{(b,a'):b|_A=a'|_A\}$ with coordinatewise ring operations. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $S$ be a commutative $R$-algebra flat over $R$, and put $S_B=S\otimes_R B$, $S_{A'}=S\otimes_R A'$ and $S_A=S\otimes_R A$. Let $N$ be an $S_B$-module finitely presented over $S_B$ and flat over $B$, and let $M'$ be an $S_{A'}$-module finitely presented over $S_{A'}$ and flat over $A'$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Given an $S_A$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'} A$, put $M=M'\otimes_{A'} A$ and form $P=N\times_M M'$ using the maps induced by $\varphi$ and scalar extension. Then $P$, with its coordinatewise $S$-action, is finitely presented over $S$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $R\to S$, no finite-generation hypothesis on $I$, and no nilpotence or Noetherian assumption is imposed; zero rings and modules are allowed.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, case of a flat ambient algebra (factorization S = S in hypothesis (3)), in Situation 08KH (situation-module-over-fibre-product).

proof.text: Apply the second assertion of [lem-sfb-flat-module-fibre-product-patching] to the flat $R$-module $S$. It identifies $S$ with $S_B\times_{S_A}S_{A'}$ by $s\mapsto(s\otimes1,s\otimes1)$. This map preserves multiplication and the unit, so the identification is one of rings. Tensor the exact sequence $I\to A'\to A\to0$ with $S$ over $R$: [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] gives $S_{A'}\twoheadrightarrow S_A$ with kernel $IS_{A'}$. Thus the new square is another surjective ring pullback, without any finiteness assumption on $I$.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: For any $S_B$-module $U$, the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $U\otimes_{S_B}S_A\cong U\otimes_B A$: the maps are $u\otimes(s\otimes a)\mapsto su\otimes a$ and $u\otimes a\mapsto u\otimes(1\otimes a)$. They respect the balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors. The same formulas with $A'$ in place of $B$ give $V\otimes_{S_{A'}}S_A\cong V\otimes_{A'}A$ for any $S_{A'}$-module $V$. They commute with module maps, since both compositions send a pure tensor to the image of its module factor times the same scalar. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], the latter tensor for $V=M'$ is $M'/(IS_{A'})M'$. Consequently the given $\varphi$ makes $(N,M')$ a module-patching datum over the square in step 1, with the same fibre product $P$.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: A finite presentation gives finite generators by taking the images of the standard basis in its last finite free term [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Therefore $N$ is finite over $S_B$ and $M'$ is finite over $S_{A'}$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-module-fibre-product-patching] to the ring square of step 1 and the datum of step 2. It follows that $P$ is finite over $S$. Choose generators $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ and let $q:S^n\twoheadrightarrow P$ send $(s_i)$ to $\sum_i s_ip_i$; set $K=\ker q$.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: The canonical component maps identify $P\otimes_S S_B$ with $N$ and $P\otimes_S S_{A'}$ with $M'$ by [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change], applied to the same surjective square. Tensor $q$ with each component ring. Right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] makes the resulting maps $q_B:S_B^n\twoheadrightarrow N$ and $q_{A'}:S_{A'}^n\twoheadrightarrow M'$ surjective. Here the free-module tensor identifications send $e_i\otimes t$ to $te_i$, with inverse $(t_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes t_i$, by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $K_B=\ker q_B$, $K_{A'}=\ker q_{A'}$, and let $q_A:S_A^n\to M$ be the common scalar extension of these maps, using $\varphi$; put $K_A=\ker q_A$. The two maps agree because each sends the $i$th basis vector to the common image of the two components of $p_i$.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: The sources $S_B^n$ and $S_{A'}^n$ are finitely generated by their standard bases; the targets $N$ and $M'$ are finitely presented by hypothesis. Hence [lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel], applied separately over $S_B$ and $S_{A'}$ to the surjections in step 4, says that $K_B$ is finite over $S_B$ and $K_{A'}$ is finite over $S_{A'}$.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: Regard $0\to K_B\to S_B^n\to N\to0$ as a short exact sequence of $B$-modules. Since its quotient $N$ is flat over $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] says that tensoring it with $A$ over $B$ stays short exact. Under the explicit tensor identifications of steps 2 and 4 this sequence is $0\to K_B\otimes_B A\to S_A^n\xrightarrow{q_A}M\to0$. Thus $K_B\otimes_B A\cong K_A$ by the map induced by the inclusion of $K_B$. The same argument over $A'$, using the flatness of the quotient $M'$ over $A'$, gives $K_{A'}\otimes_{A'} A\cong K_A$. These are $S_A$-linear isomorphisms: multiplication by $s\otimes a$ acts by multiplication by $s$ on the original kernel and by $a$ on the tensor factor, and the inclusions commute with that action. The balancing formulas of step 2 identify these with $K_B\otimes_{S_B}S_A\cong K_A\cong K_{A'}\otimes_{S_{A'}}S_A$. Hence the kernels form a compatible module-patching datum over step 1's square.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: The ring identification of step 1 gives the coordinatewise identification $S^n=S_B^n\times_{S_A^n}S_{A'}^n$. Its restriction identifies $K$ with $K_B\times_{K_A}K_{A'}$: if $x\in K$, its two components are killed by $q_B,q_{A'}$ and have the same reduction. Conversely, a pair in $K_B\times_{K_A}K_{A'}$ has equal images in $S_A^n$, since both embeddings of $K_A$ are the kernel inclusion in $S_A^n$. It therefore comes from a unique $x\in S^n$. Both components of $q(x)$ vanish; since $P=N\times_M M'$ is literally a set of pairs, $q(x)=0$. These two restrictions are inverse and $S$-linear.

source.place: Tag 08KP, lemma-relative-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product, proof after “Assume B′ → D′ is flat”.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-module-fibre-product-patching] again over the square of step 1, now to the kernel datum of step 6. The component kernels are finite by step 5, so $K_B\times_{K_A}K_{A'}$, and hence $K$, is finite over $S$. Choose $m$ generators of $K$. Their inclusions in $S^n$ define a map $S^m\to S^n$ with image exactly $K$. Therefore $S^m\to S^n\xrightarrow{q}P\to0$ is exact, which is a finite presentation by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].
